title: Surrogate Modeling for the Design of Optimal Lattice Structures using Tensor Completion
experiments_summary: The study used the lattice structure dataset from Gongora et al., where mechanical performance is characterized by Young's modulus (E) and the ratio of E to mass (Ẽ). Each design parameter was mapped to a mode of a tensor, and tensor completion was applied to predict unobserved entries. Two experimental settings were evaluated: (1) uniform random sampling of the training set, with varying training sizes and 5 repeated iterations per size to report mean and standard deviation on a held-out test set; and (2) biased (non-uniform) random sampling, simulating an experimentalist who samples some regions of the design space more than others. In the biased setting, the number of training samples per unit cell geometry type was drawn from an exponential distribution (scale=1) and mapped to a range [l, 40], where l increased across 10 experiments from 3 to 21, progressively reducing sampling bias. Tensor completion models used were CPD-S (with smoothness constraints, ranks 1, 2, 4), NeAT (rank 24 and 32), and an ensemble of these models aggregated via a random forest regressor (100 trees). All tensor models were trained with the Adam optimizer (learning rate and weight decay both 0.01) using Mean Absolute Error as the objective. Baseline methods compared included XGBoost, MLPs, and Gaussian Process models (with kernel = ConstantKernel × RBF + WhiteKernel and alpha=0.01, selected empirically); only Gaussian Process results are reported as it was the best-performing baseline. Performance was evaluated via MAE on the test set across both sampling conditions and multiple training sizes.
